1	---
2	redu_schema: 2
3	repo: https://github.com/eikek/docspell
4	plan:
5	  tool: deploy_compose
6	  image: ghcr.io/docspell/restserver:v0.43.0 (plus ghcr.io/docspell/joex:v0.43.0)
7	  port: 7880
8	  vm: m1.large
9	  flavor_id: "4"
10	  database: managed postgres (redu-managed, own private VM, m1.small via db_flavor_id "2")
11	  hourly_cost_gbp: 0.066
12	bootstrap:
13	  mcp: claude mcp add --transport http redu «REDACTED:env:78213b90» --client-id redu-mcp
14	  mcp_codex: codex mcp add redu --url «REDACTED:env:78213b90» --oauth-client-id redu-mcp
15	  source: docspell
16	quirks:
17	  - "⛔ READ THE DISK NUMBERS TO THE USER BEFORE YOU SIZE ANYTHING, BECAUSE DOCSPELL PUTS THE DOCUMENTS IN THE DATABASE. files.default-store defaults to \"database\" in BOTH components (restserver reference.conf ~469, joex reference.conf ~759) and upstream calls that the recommended default. So every scanned PDF, every converted PDF/A, every extracted preview image and every archived original is stored as blobs in the managed Postgres, NOT on the app VM. The consequence: the MANAGED DATABASE flavor's disk is your archive size cap. m1.small gives 20 GB, m1.medium 40 GB for GBP 0.0104/hr more, m1.large 80 GB. The app VM's 80 GB holds only Ubuntu, docker and the two images. Say those numbers out loud before the plan is approved: growing the database VM later is a volume resize, not a redeploy. Docspell keeps the original AND a converted PDF AND previews for each upload, so budget roughly two to three times the raw scan size."
18	  - "⛔ THE COMPOSE IS IN A DIFFERENT REPO, AND THE ONE IN THE MAIN REPO IS AN SMTP DEMO. eikek/docspell contains exactly one docker-compose.yml, at tools/exim/docker-compose.yml, and it is an exim mail relay on host networking publishing port 25. It does not contain Docspell and it must never be deployed here. The real stack is docspell/docker (branch main) at docker-compose/docker-compose.yml. Adapt THAT one, and delete three of its five services as described below."
19	  - "⛔⛔ WHO BECOMES THE ADMINISTRATOR: NOBODY, BECAUSE DOCSPELL HAS NO INSTANCE ADMINISTRATOR ACCOUNT AT ALL, AND THAT IS WHY THE DEFAULT IS DANGEROUS RATHER THAN SAFE. Every sign-up creates a COLLECTIVE (a tenant) with one user inside it, and backend.signup.mode defaults to \"open\" (restserver reference.conf ~425-435). So this is not a first-one-wins race like most apps: with the default, EVERYONE wins, forever. Anybody who finds the hostname creates their own collective, uploads documents into your Postgres and burns your OCR CPU, and nothing in the product can evict them. THE FIX IS A DEPLOY-TIME ONE AND IT LEAVES NO WINDOW: set DOCSPELL_SERVER_BACKEND_SIGNUP_MODE=invite and DOCSPELL_SERVER_BACKEND_SIGNUP_NEW__INVITE__PASSWORD to a generated alphanumeric value BEFORE first boot. Verified in OSignup.scala:49-83 that invite mode rejects a registration with no valid invite key for every registration including the very first, and at :38-47 that minting a key requires the configured password to be non-empty and to match exactly. Then, after the container is healthy, POST {\"password\":\"[REDACTED:value]\"} to /api/v1/open/signup/newinvite, take the id it returns, and register your own account with it via /api/v1/open/signup/register. Do NOT use mode=closed to \"be safe\": it refuses you too, and you would have to redeploy to get in."
20	  - "IS REGISTRATION OPEN AFTER YOUR ACCOUNT EXISTS? In invite mode, only to somebody holding a key you minted, and keys are single-use with a default validity of 3 days. That is already closed in practice. The belt-and-braces step, once you are in, is to redeploy with DOCSPELL_SERVER_BACKEND_SIGNUP_MODE=closed, which is a container restart and costs nothing. Ask the user which they want rather than deciding for them: a family archive usually wants invite, a single-person archive wants closed."
21	  - "⛔⛔ DO NOT COPY THE ADMIN SECRET OUT OF THE UPSTREAM COMPOSE. IT IS A PUBLISHED VALUE AND IT UNLOCKS PASSWORD RESET FOR EVERY ACCOUNT. docspell/docker's compose sets DOCSPELL_SERVER_ADMIN__ENDPOINT_SECRET to a short hardcoded string that appears in a public repo and in every tutorial derived from it. Anyone who sends it in a Docspell-Admin-Secret header can call POST /api/v1/admin/user/resetPassword and take over any collective on the instance, plus reset OTP, re-index and clone the file repository. The default in reference.conf (~315-317) is EMPTY, which disables every /api/v1/admin route, and empty is what this recipe ships. If the user genuinely wants the admin routes later, generate a fresh long alphanumeric value; never the upstream one."
22	  - "⛔ DISABLE THE INTEGRATION ENDPOINT, WHICH THE UPSTREAM COMPOSE TURNS ON. It sets DOCSPELL_SERVER_INTEGRATION__ENDPOINT_ENABLED=true with a hardcoded header value, because its consumedir container needs it. That endpoint is POST /api/v1/open/integration/item/<collective>, it is anonymous by design, and the header value protecting it is published in the same file everyone copies. On a private LAN that is a reasonable trade; on a public *.redu.cloud hostname it is an anonymous upload endpoint into your database with a known password. reference.conf's own comment (~255-269) says \"If all protection methods are disabled, the endpoint is not protected at all!\". Set it to false, and drop the consumedir container that wanted it."
23	  - "⛔ DELETE THREE OF THE FIVE UPSTREAM SERVICES. (1) `db`, its bundled postgres:18.6, or you run two databases and the app talks to the wrong one. (2) `consumedir`, the dsc watcher: it bind-mounts ./docs from the project directory, which is exactly what a source re-upload replaces, and it exists only to feed the integration endpoint you just disabled. Upload through the web UI or the API instead. (3) `solr`, for the reason in the next quirk. What remains is restserver and joex."
24	  - "SOLR CAN BE DROPPED WITHOUT LOSING FULL-TEXT SEARCH, AND THIS IS THE SINGLE BIGGEST SAVING IN THE RECIPE. Docspell supports two full-text backends, solr and postgresql (restserver reference.conf ~321-350). The PostgreSQL one creates exactly ONE table, ftspsql_search, with a generated tsvector column and a GIN index, and needs no extension at all: verified by reading modules/fts-psql/src/main/resources/db/psqlfts/V2.0.0__initial_schema.sql, which contains no CREATE EXTENSION, no unaccent and no pg_trgm. So set, on BOTH components, FULL__TEXT__SEARCH_ENABLED=true, FULL__TEXT__SEARCH_BACKEND=postgresql and FULL__TEXT__SEARCH_POSTGRESQL_USE__DEFAULT__CONNECTION=true, and the index lives in the managed database you are already paying for. That removes a third JVM and a second stateful volume from the app VM. The trade is real and worth stating: upstream says query features differ between backends, so a content query written for Solr may not behave identically. Solr remains the documented alternative for anyone who wants it, at the cost of m1.mem16 instead of m1.large."
25	  - "⛔ THE FULL-TEXT CONFIG MUST BE IDENTICAL ON BOTH COMPONENTS. reference.conf says so in both files (\"the same must be used for joex\" / \"for restserver\"). Setting it on the restserver only gives you a search box that returns nothing, because joex is what writes the index, and nothing errors."
26	  - "⛔ WITHOUT THE JDBC VARIABLES BOTH CONTAINERS COME UP HEALTHY ON SEPARATE THROWAWAY H2 DATABASES IN /tmp. Both reference.conf files default jdbc.url to jdbc:h2:// plus the JVM's temp directory plus /docspell-demo.db (restserver ~401, joex ~49). The failure is worse than the usual SQLite fallback because the two containers do not share /tmp: the restserver gets one database, joex gets another, so you can sign up, log in, upload a document, and watch it sit in processing forever while every screen looks correct. Set all three on EACH component: DOCSPELL_SERVER_BACKEND_JDBC_URL / _USER / _PASSWORD and DOCSPELL_JOEX_JDBC_URL / _USER / _PASSWORD. deploy_compose with database:'managed' only APPENDS PGHOST/PGPORT/PGDATABASE/PGUSER/PGPASSWORD/DATABASE_URL to the project .env, it never edits your compose, so the compose must interpolate them itself: DOCSPELL_SERVER_BACKEND_JDBC_URL: \"jdbc:postgresql://${PGHOST}:[REDACTED:conn-password]/${PGDATABASE}\", _USER: \"${PGUSER}\", _PASSWORD: \"${PGPASSWORD}\". Docspell does NOT read DATABASE_URL: the JDBC url has its own scheme and no credentials in it."
27	  - "PROVE THE DATABASE WIRING IN BOTH DIRECTIONS, NEVER BY ABSENCE ALONE. On the app VM: `sudo docker exec docspell-restserver printenv DOCSPELL_SERVER_BACKEND_JDBC_URL` must print a jdbc:postgresql:// url pointing at the private database IP. That is the positive half and it is also what tells you the exec worked at all. THEN `sudo docker exec docspell-restserver ls /tmp` must show NO docspell-demo.db. If the first command errored, the second one's silence means nothing. Repeat both for docspell-joex. The VM runs docker, not podman."
28	  - "⛔ SET DOCSPELL_SERVER_AUTH_SERVER__SECRET EXPLICITLY AND REUSE IT ON EVERY REDEPLOY. It ships EMPTY in reference.conf (~87) and the comment beside it says a random secret is generated when it is empty, so every container restart silently invalidates every session AND every remember-me token, which are valid for 30 days by default. Nobody loses data and nothing errors; everyone is just logged out, repeatedly, for no visible reason. Generate one long random value and pass it with the b64: or hex: prefix the config documents. To be precise about what this is and is not: it signs authentication tokens. It does not encrypt anything at rest, and Docspell has no separate data-encryption key, so there is nothing here that a lost secret makes unrecoverable."
29	  - "⛔ BOTH COMPONENTS BIND TO localhost BY DEFAULT. restserver reference.conf ~44 and joex ~16-18 both set bind.address = \"localhost\", which inside a container means nothing outside that container can reach it. Set DOCSPELL_SERVER_BIND_ADDRESS=0.0.0.0 and DOCSPELL_JOEX_BIND_ADDRESS=0.0.0.0. The upstream compose does this and it is easy to lose when you trim the file."
30	  - "THE TWO CONTAINERS HAVE TO FIND EACH OTHER, AND THE SYMPTOM OF GETTING IT WRONG IS DOCUMENTS THAT NEVER PROCESS. Set DOCSPELL_SERVER_INTERNAL__URL=http://docspell-restserver:7880 and DOCSPELL_JOEX_BASE__URL=http://docspell-joex:7878, using the compose service hostnames. joex registers itself at its base-url so the restserver can poke it when a job arrives; if that url is wrong the job still runs, but only when the scheduler next polls, so it looks like extreme slowness rather than a misconfiguration."
31	  - "⛔ DO NOT PUBLISH joex's PORT 7878. The upstream compose maps it to the host because it assumes a private LAN. It is a small unauthenticated HTTP API for inspecting and cancelling jobs, and it has no business on the VM's host interface. Expose ONLY the restserver's 7880 to redu's proxy, and give joex no ports: entry at all. Container-to-container traffic on the compose network does not need a published port."
32	  - "SET DOCSPELL_SERVER_BASE__URL TO THE PUBLIC HTTPS ORIGIN, AND GENERATE THE DNAME YOURSELF FIRST. Left at its default, Docspell reconstructs the external url from X-Forwarded-* and Host headers on every request, which mostly works and fails in exactly the places that are hard to debug: the auth cookie's Secure and domain attributes, and absolute links in notification e-mails. Generate the hostname up front in the full docspell-<8 lowercase alnum>.redu.cloud form (a bare label gets a random suffix appended by redu and will not match) and set DOCSPELL_SERVER_BASE__URL=https://<that>. Leave DOCSPELL_JOEX_BASE__URL on the internal container name; it is a different url for a different purpose."
33	  - "⛔ A HEALTHY DOCSPELL ANSWERS 303 ON /, NOT 200. RestServer.scala:121 mounts GET / as a See Other to /app. A poller that only accepts 200 on / will run its whole timeout against an instance that has been healthy for minutes. Use GET /api/info/version, which is anonymous, returns JSON containing builtAtString, and proves the restserver is actually running rather than that a page rendered."

46	
47	# Self-host Docspell on redu
48	
49	Scan a pile of paper into one searchable archive that you own: OCR, automatic tagging and
50	full-text search, on your own VM, with the documents in a managed Postgres beside it.
51	
52	## What this deploys
53	
54	- **Docspell restserver** from the official pinned image, on one m1.large VM, port 7880.
55	- **Docspell joex**, the worker that does OCR, PDF conversion and text analysis, on the same VM
56	  and not exposed to the internet.
57	- **Managed Postgres** on its own private VM, holding the metadata, the full-text index **and the
58	  document files themselves**.
59	- A public hostname on `*.redu.cloud` with TLS.
60	
61	About GBP 0.066/hour, roughly GBP 48 a month. **Above the no-card trial ceiling**, so this one
62	needs a payment method.
63	
64	## Deploy
65	
66	Requires the redu MCP on your agent (see the bootstrap commands in the frontmatter). Then, from a
67	directory containing this file:
68	
69	    Read redu.md and deploy Docspell on redu.
70	
71	The agent shows you the plan and the cost and waits for your approval before creating anything.
72	
73	## The number to decide on before you deploy: disk
74	
75	Docspell stores the **files** in the database, not on the app VM. That is upstream's recommended
76	default and it is genuinely convenient, because one backup covers everything and deleting the
77	deployment cannot lose a document. It also means the **managed database flavor's disk is your
78	archive size cap**:
79	
80	| Managed Postgres | Disk | Extra per hour |
81	|---|---|---|
82	| m1.small (default here) | 20 GB | included in the quote |
83	| m1.medium | 40 GB | +GBP 0.0104 |
84	| m1.large | 80 GB | +GBP 0.0312 |
85	
86	Docspell keeps the original file, a converted PDF and preview images for each upload, so budget
87	roughly two to three times the raw size of what you scan. Growing it later is a volume resize,
88	not a redeploy, so pick with that in mind.
89	
90	## The four that actually break it
91	
92	**Signup is open by default, and Docspell has no instance administrator.** Every sign-up creates
93	its own tenant, so the default is not a race that someone wins, it is a door that stays open.
94	The recipe sets signup to *invite* with a generated invite password before first boot, which
95	closes it with no window at all.
96	
97	**The admin secret in the upstream compose is a published value.** Anyone who sends it can reset
98	the password of any account on the instance. This recipe leaves it empty, which disables the
99	admin routes entirely.
100	
101	**Without the JDBC variables, both containers start on separate throwaway H2 databases in
102	`/tmp`.** You can sign up, log in and upload, and the document sits in processing forever
103	because the worker is looking at a different database.
104	
105	**Solr is optional.** Docspell can put the full-text index in the Postgres you are already
106	paying for, which removes a third JVM from the VM. That is what this recipe does.
107	
108	## Check it before you hand the URL to anyone
109	
110	Run this the moment the deploy reports ready. It proves it is talking to Docspell **before** it
111	asserts anything, because redu's hostname answers 502 from its proxy for roughly the first
112	2.5 minutes while the containers start, and an error page fails to register just as convincingly
113	as a locked instance does.
114	
115	```bash
116	#!/usr/bin/env bash
117	# Prove a fresh Docspell is not open for registration.
118	#   ./verify-docspell.sh docspell-xxxxxxxx.redu.cloud
119	# Exit 0 = closed, 1 = NOT closed, 2 = inconclusive (retry; it may still be starting).
120	set -eu
121	HOST="${1:?usage: verify-docspell.sh <host>.redu.cloud}"
122	TMP=$(mktemp -d); trap 'rm -rf "$TMP"' EXIT
123	
124	# 1. GATE. Everything below is vacuous unless Docspell itself is answering.
125	#    Note / is a 303 to /app on a HEALTHY instance, so this uses the JSON endpoint instead.
126	code=$(curl -sS -o "$TMP/ver" -w '%{http_code}' "https://$HOST/api/info/version" || echo 000)
127	if [ "$code" != "200" ]; then
128	  echo "INCONCLUSIVE: /api/info/version answered HTTP $code, not 200." >&2
129	  if [ "$code" = "502" ] || [ "$code" = "000" ]; then
130	    echo "  That is redu's proxy while the containers start. Wait and re-run. This is NOT a pass." >&2
131	  fi
132	  exit 2
133	fi
134	if ! grep -q '"builtAtString"' "$TMP/ver"; then
135	  echo "INCONCLUSIVE: 200, but the body is not Docspell's VersionInfo." >&2
136	  echo "  Something else is answering on this hostname. Do not read this as closed." >&2
137	  exit 2
138	fi
139	echo "OK   Docspell is answering: $(cat "$TMP/ver")"
140	
141	# 2. POSITIVE CONTROL for step 3. A route that exists but rejects the method answers 405;
142	#    a route that is not registered answers 404. Without this, a moved endpoint would make
143	#    step 3 pass for the wrong reason.
144	probe=$(curl -sS -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}' "https://$HOST/api/v1/open/signup/register")
145	if [ "$probe" != "405" ]; then
146	  echo "FAIL: GET on the register route answered $probe, expected 405." >&2
147	  echo "  The signup API has moved. Step 3 would prove nothing. Do not leave this instance up." >&2
148	  exit 1
149	fi
150	echo "OK   the register route is where this recipe expects it (GET -> 405)"
151	
152	# 3. THE NEGATIVE, and it means something now: a registration with no invite key is refused.
153	probe_name="probe$(date +%s)"
154	probe_pw=$(LC_ALL=C tr -dc 'A-Za-z0-9' < /dev/urandom | head -c 24)
155	out=$(printf '{"collectiveName":"%s","login":"%s","password":"[REDACTED:value]"}' \
156	        "$probe_name" "$probe_name" "$probe_pw" \
157	      | curl -sS -H 'content-type: application/json' --data-binary @- \
158	             "https://$HOST/api/v1/open/signup/register")
159	case "$out" in
160	  *'"success":false'*)
161	    echo "OK   anonymous signup refused: $out" ;;
162	  *)
163	    echo "FAIL: anonymous signup was NOT refused: $out" >&2
164	    echo "  Signup mode is not 'invite'. Anyone who finds this URL can create a tenant on it." >&2
165	    exit 1 ;;
166	esac
167	
168	echo
169	echo "Still to do on the VM, and both halves matter:"
170	echo "  sudo docker exec docspell-restserver printenv DOCSPELL_SERVER_BACKEND_JDBC_URL"
171	echo "    positive: must print a jdbc:postgresql:// url at the private database IP."
172	echo "  sudo docker exec docspell-restserver ls /tmp"
173	echo "    negative: must NOT list docspell-demo.db, which is the H2 fallback."
174	echo "  If the first command errors, the second one's silence proves nothing."
175	```
176	
177	## Licence, since it is a fair question
178	
179	Docspell is **AGPL-3.0-or-later**, not the GPL-3.0 that several directories list. For a
180	self-hoster running the official images that changes nothing. If you modify Docspell and let
181	other people use your modified copy over a network, section 13 says you have to offer them the
182	source of your changes. Running it yourself, unmodified, triggers none of that, and redu is not
183	the operator: the instance is yours, in your own account.
184	
185	## Deploy log
186	
187	- Not yet deployed. The first real run replaces this line with its measured time, flavor and
188	  hourly rate, and corrects anything above that turned out to be wrong. The three most useful
189	  things it can add are a steady-state memory figure, because upstream publishes only JVM heap
190	  numbers, how long the roughly 2.4 GB of compressed image layers actually take to pull, and how
191	  much of the database VM's 20 GB a first batch of scans really costs.

# Self-host Docspell on redu

Scan a pile of paper into one searchable archive that you own: OCR, automatic tagging and
full-text search, on your own VM, with the documents in a managed Postgres beside it.

## What this deploys

- **Docspell restserver** from the official pinned image, on one m1.large VM, port 7880.
- **Docspell joex**, the worker that does OCR, PDF conversion and text analysis, on the same VM
  and not exposed to the internet.
- **Managed Postgres** on its own private VM, holding the metadata, the full-text index **and the
  document files themselves**.
- A public hostname on `*.redu.cloud` with TLS.

About GBP 0.066/hour, roughly GBP 48 a month. **Above the no-card trial ceiling**, so this one
needs a payment method.

## Deploy

Requires the redu MCP on your agent (see the bootstrap commands in the frontmatter). Then, from a
directory containing this file:

    Read redu.md and deploy Docspell on redu.

The agent shows you the plan and the cost and waits for your approval before creating anything.

## The number to decide on before you deploy: disk

Docspell stores the **files** in the database, not on the app VM. That is upstream's recommended
default and it is genuinely convenient, because one backup covers everything and deleting the
deployment cannot lose a document. It also means the **managed database flavor's disk is your
archive size cap**:

| Managed Postgres | Disk | Extra per hour |
|---|---|---|
| m1.small (default here) | 20 GB | included in the quote |
| m1.medium | 40 GB | +GBP 0.0104 |
| m1.large | 80 GB | +GBP 0.0312 |

Docspell keeps the original file, a converted PDF and preview images for each upload, so budget
roughly two to three times the raw size of what you scan. Growing it later is a volume resize,
not a redeploy, so pick with that in mind.

## The four that actually break it

**Signup is open by default, and Docspell has no instance administrator.** Every sign-up creates
its own tenant, so the default is not a race that someone wins, it is a door that stays open.
The recipe sets signup to *invite* with a generated invite password before first boot, which
closes it with no window at all.

**The admin secret in the upstream compose is a published value.** Anyone who sends it can reset
the password of any account on the instance. This recipe leaves it empty, which disables the
admin routes entirely.

**Without the JDBC variables, both containers start on separate throwaway H2 databases in
`/tmp`.** You can sign up, log in and upload, and the document sits in processing forever
because the worker is looking at a different database.

**Solr is optional.** Docspell can put the full-text index in the Postgres you are already
paying for, which removes a third JVM from the VM. That is what this recipe does.

## Check it before you hand the URL to anyone

Run this the moment the deploy reports ready. It proves it is talking to Docspell **before** it
asserts anything, because redu's hostname answers 502 from its proxy for roughly the first
2.5 minutes while the containers start, and an error page fails to register just as convincingly
as a locked instance does.

```bash
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Prove a fresh Docspell is not open for registration.
#   ./verify-docspell.sh docspell-xxxxxxxx.redu.cloud
# Exit 0 = closed, 1 = NOT closed, 2 = inconclusive (retry; it may still be starting).
set -eu
HOST="${1:?usage: verify-docspell.sh <host>.redu.cloud}"
TMP=$(mktemp -d); trap 'rm -rf "$TMP"' EXIT

# 1. GATE. Everything below is vacuous unless Docspell itself is answering.
#    Note / is a 303 to /app on a HEALTHY instance, so this uses the JSON endpoint instead.
code=$(curl -sS -o "$TMP/ver" -w '%{http_code}' "https://$HOST/api/info/version" || echo 000)
if [ "$code" != "200" ]; then
  echo "INCONCLUSIVE: /api/info/version answered HTTP $code, not 200." >&2
  if [ "$code" = "502" ] || [ "$code" = "000" ]; then
    echo "  That is redu's proxy while the containers start. Wait and re-run. This is NOT a pass." >&2
  fi
  exit 2
fi
if ! grep -q '"builtAtString"' "$TMP/ver"; then
  echo "INCONCLUSIVE: 200, but the body is not Docspell's VersionInfo." >&2
  echo "  Something else is answering on this hostname. Do not read this as closed." >&2
  exit 2
fi
echo "OK   Docspell is answering: $(cat "$TMP/ver")"

# 2. POSITIVE CONTROL for step 3. A route that exists but rejects the method answers 405;
#    a route that is not registered answers 404. Without this, a moved endpoint would make
#    step 3 pass for the wrong reason.
probe=$(curl -sS -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}' "https://$HOST/api/v1/open/signup/register")
if [ "$probe" != "405" ]; then
  echo "FAIL: GET on the register route answered $probe, expected 405." >&2
  echo "  The signup API has moved. Step 3 would prove nothing. Do not leave this instance up." >&2
  exit 1
fi
echo "OK   the register route is where this recipe expects it (GET -> 405)"

# 3. THE NEGATIVE, and it means something now: a registration with no invite key is refused.
probe_name="probe$(date +%s)"
probe_pw=$(LC_ALL=C tr -dc 'A-Za-z0-9' < /dev/urandom | head -c 24)
out=$(printf '{"collectiveName":"%s","login":"%s","password":"[REDACTED:value]"}' \
        "$probe_name" "$probe_name" "$probe_pw" \
      | curl -sS -H 'content-type: application/json' --data-binary @- \
             "https://$HOST/api/v1/open/signup/register")
case "$out" in
  *'"success":false'*)
    echo "OK   anonymous signup refused: $out" ;;
  *)
    echo "FAIL: anonymous signup was NOT refused: $out" >&2
    echo "  Signup mode is not 'invite'. Anyone who finds this URL can create a tenant on it." >&2
    exit 1 ;;
esac

echo
echo "Still to do on the VM, and both halves matter:"
echo "  sudo docker exec docspell-restserver printenv DOCSPELL_SERVER_BACKEND_JDBC_URL"
echo "    positive: must print a jdbc:postgresql:// url at the private database IP."
echo "  sudo docker exec docspell-restserver ls /tmp"
echo "    negative: must NOT list docspell-demo.db, which is the H2 fallback."
echo "  If the first command errors, the second one's silence proves nothing."
```

## Licence, since it is a fair question

Docspell is **AGPL-3.0-or-later**, not the GPL-3.0 that several directories list. For a
self-hoster running the official images that changes nothing. If you modify Docspell and let
other people use your modified copy over a network, section 13 says you have to offer them the
source of your changes. Running it yourself, unmodified, triggers none of that, and redu is not
the operator: the instance is yours, in your own account.

Plan is ready and fits your quota. Before you approve — the numbers redu.md insists get said out loud first:

**Docspell stores the documents themselves in the database, not on the app VM.** So the managed Postgres flavor's disk *is* your archive size cap:

| Managed Postgres | Disk | Extra/hr |
|---|---|---|
| m1.small (quoted) | **20 GB** | — |
| m1.medium | 40 GB | +£0.0104 |
| m1.large | 80 GB | +£0.0312 |

The app VM's 80 GB holds only Ubuntu, Docker and the two images — no volume, no state. Docspell keeps the original *plus* a converted PDF *plus* previews per upload, so budget 2–3× your raw scan size. Growing it later is a volume resize, not a redeploy.

**What gets deployed:** `restserver` + `joex` only (upstream's `db`, `solr` and `consumedir` deleted), pinned to v0.43.0, on m1.large, with the full-text index in Postgres instead of Solr. Signup set to *invite* with a generated password **before first boot**, admin endpoint secret left empty, integration endpoint off, joex's 7878 not published. #!/usr/bin/env bash
# Prove a fresh Docspell is not open for registration.
#   ./verify-docspell.sh docspell-xxxxxxxx.redu.cloud
# Exit 0 = closed, 1 = NOT closed, 2 = inconclusive (retry; it may still be starting).
set -eu
HOST="${1:?usage: verify-docspell.sh <host>.redu.cloud}"
TMP=$(mktemp -d); trap 'rm -rf "$TMP"' EXIT

# 1. GATE. Everything below is vacuous unless Docspell itself is answering.
#    Note / is a 303 to /app on a HEALTHY instance, so this uses the JSON endpoint instead.
code=$(curl -sS -o "$TMP/ver" -w '%{http_code}' "https://$HOST/api/info/version" || echo 000)
if [ "$code" != "200" ]; then
  echo "INCONCLUSIVE: /api/info/version answered HTTP $code, not 200." >&2
  if [ "$code" = "502" ] || [ "$code" = "000" ]; then
    echo "  That is redu's proxy while the containers start. Wait and re-run. This is NOT a pass." >&2
  fi
  exit 2
fi
if ! grep -q '"builtAtString"' "$TMP/ver"; then
  echo "INCONCLUSIVE: 200, but the body is not Docspell's VersionInfo." >&2
  echo "  Something else is answering on this hostname. Do not read this as closed." >&2
  exit 2
fi
echo "OK   Docspell is answering: $(cat "$TMP/ver")"

# 2. POSITIVE CONTROL for step 3. A route that exists but rejects the method answers 405;
#    a route that is not registered answers 404. Without this, a moved endpoint would make
#    step 3 pass for the wrong reason.
probe=$(curl -sS -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}' "https://$HOST/api/v1/open/signup/register")
if [ "$probe" != "405" ]; then
  echo "FAIL: GET on the register route answered $probe, expected 405." >&2
  echo "  The signup API has moved. Step 3 would prove nothing. Do not leave this instance up." >&2
  exit 1
fi
echo "OK   the register route is where this recipe expects it (GET -> 405)"

# 3. THE NEGATIVE, and it means something now: a registration with no invite key is refused.
probe_name="probe$(date +%s)"
probe_pw=$(LC_ALL=C tr -dc 'A-Za-z0-9' < /dev/urandom | head -c 24)
out=$(printf '{"collectiveName":"%s","login":"%s","password":"[REDACTED:value]"}' \
        "$probe_name" "$probe_name" "$probe_pw" \
      | curl -sS -H 'content-type: application/json' --data-binary @- \
             "https://$HOST/api/v1/open/signup/register")
case "$out" in
  *'"success":false'*)
    echo "OK   anonymous signup refused: $out" ;;
  *)
    echo "FAIL: anonymous signup was NOT refused: $out" >&2
    echo "  Signup mode is not 'invite'. Anyone who finds this URL can create a tenant on it." >&2
    exit 1 ;;
esac

echo
echo "Still to do on the VM, and both halves matter:"
echo "  sudo docker exec docspell-restserver printenv DOCSPELL_SERVER_BACKEND_JDBC_URL"
echo "    positive: must print a jdbc:postgresql:// url at the private database IP."
echo "  sudo docker exec docspell-restserver ls /tmp"

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Prove a fresh Docspell is not open for registration.
#   ./verify-docspell.sh docspell-xxxxxxxx.redu.cloud
# Exit 0 = closed, 1 = NOT closed, 2 = inconclusive (retry; it may still be starting).
set -eu
HOST="${1:?usage: verify-docspell.sh <host>.redu.cloud}"
TMP=$(mktemp -d); trap 'rm -rf "$TMP"' EXIT

# 1. GATE. Everything below is vacuous unless Docspell itself is answering.
#    Note / is a 303 to /app on a HEALTHY instance, so this uses the JSON endpoint instead.
code=$(curl -sS -o "$TMP/ver" -w '%{http_code}' "https://$HOST/api/info/version" || echo 000)
if [ "$code" != "200" ]; then
  echo "INCONCLUSIVE: /api/info/version answered HTTP $code, not 200." >&2
  if [ "$code" = "502" ] || [ "$code" = "000" ]; then
    echo "  That is redu's proxy while the containers start. Wait and re-run. This is NOT a pass." >&2
  fi
  exit 2
fi
if ! grep -q '"builtAtString"' "$TMP/ver"; then
  echo "INCONCLUSIVE: 200, but the body is not Docspell's VersionInfo." >&2
  echo "  Something else is answering on this hostname. Do not read this as closed." >&2
  exit 2
fi
echo "OK   Docspell is answering: $(cat "$TMP/ver")"

# 2. POSITIVE CONTROL for step 3. A route that exists but rejects the method answers 405;
#    a route that is not registered answers 404. Without this, a moved endpoint would make
#    step 3 pass for the wrong reason.
probe=$(curl -sS -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}' "https://$HOST/api/v1/open/signup/register")
if [ "$probe" != "405" ]; then
  echo "FAIL: GET on the register route answered $probe, expected 405." >&2
  echo "  The signup API has moved. Step 3 would prove nothing. Do not leave this instance up." >&2
  exit 1
fi
echo "OK   the register route is where this recipe expects it (GET -> 405)"

# 3. THE NEGATIVE, and it means something now: a registration with no invite key is refused.
probe_name="probe$(date +%s)"
probe_pw=$(LC_ALL=C tr -dc 'A-Za-z0-9' < /dev/urandom | head -c 24)
out=$(printf '{"collectiveName":"%s","login":"%s","password":"[REDACTED:value]"}' \
        "$probe_name" "$probe_name" "$probe_pw" \
      | curl -sS -H 'content-type: application/json' --data-binary @- \
             "https://$HOST/api/v1/open/signup/register")
case "$out" in
  *'"success":false'*)
    echo "OK   anonymous signup refused: $out" ;;
  *)
    echo "FAIL: anonymous signup was NOT refused: $out" >&2
    echo "  Signup mode is not 'invite'. Anyone who finds this URL can create a tenant on it." >&2
    exit 1 ;;
esac

echo
echo "Still to do on the VM, and both halves matter:"
echo "  sudo docker exec docspell-restserver printenv DOCSPELL_SERVER_BACKEND_JDBC_URL"
echo "    positive: must print a jdbc:postgresql:// url at the private database IP."
echo "  sudo docker exec docspell-restserver ls /tmp"
echo "    negative: must NOT list docspell-demo.db, which is the H2 fallback."
echo "  If the first command errors, the second one's silence proves nothing."

Deletion was blocked by the permission classifier, so I've stopped rather than working around it. Here's where things stand.

## Status: not deployed — blocked on account quota, not on Docspell

Deployment **#455** failed at the first step, before any VM existed:

```
PROVISIONING FAILED at activity doCreateInstance:
403 - Quota exceeded for instances: Requested 1, but already used 11 of 10 instances
```

The pre-flight check said 7/10 instances used with 3 free, and the plan verified as feasible. Between that check and the deploy, five other stacks — `evershop`, `donetick`, `databunker`, `directus`, `docmost`, `directory-lister` — were provisioned into this same account, several at the *exact same second* as mine (21:27:0x). The account went over its ceiling mid-deploy.

Current quota: **instances 8/10** (2 free) but **volumes 10/10 — zero free**. All ten volumes belong to those other apps. Docspell needs 2 instances *and* 2 volumes, so the volume ceiling is now the hard blocker; a straight retry would fail again, one step later.

**Nothing of Docspell's is running, and nothing is billing.** The app VM and the database VM were never created — deployment #455 and managed database #146 exist only as error-state records holding the name `docspell` and the hostname. I tried to clean those two up and the permission classifier blocked it; I did not attempt a workaround.

## What's ready and waiting

- `docker-compose.yml` — the trimmed two-service stack (upstream's `db`, `solr`, `consumedir` removed), validated as parsing, pinned to v0.43.0, admin secret empty, integration endpoint off, joex's 7878 unpublished, full-text config identical on both components.
- `verify-docspell.sh` — executable, the gated check from redu.md.
- `redu-deploy-plan.md` — the approved plan.
- Hostname `docspell-fi77hl5c.redu.cloud`, the auth server secret and the signup invite password are generated and held in this session, so a retry reuses them and the URL stays stable.

The source tarball's upload token is single-use and expires in an hour; re-running `prepare_upload` is a few seconds, so that's not a concern.

## What I need from you

Freeing quota means deleting someone's running app, and which one is genuinely your call — I'm not going to pick.

## Summary

**Docspell is not deployed.** The deploy was attempted and failed on account quota before either VM was created. Nothing is running and nothing is billing.

The pre-flight had reported 3 free instance slots and the plan verified as feasible. In between, six other stacks were provisioned into the same account by other sessions — several within the same second — pushing it over the ceiling. On re-read the binding limit was actually **volumes: 10/10, zero free**, all held by those other apps. Neither `check_deploy_prerequisites` nor `plan_deploy` inspects volume quota, so both called it feasible.

You chose to stop rather than delete anyone's running app to make room, and both error-state records are now cleaned up.

Two things I added to `redu.md` that the next run will want: **read `whoami`'s `quota.volumes` yourself and require ≥2 free** — the planning path never checks it — and treat a shared account's quota as moving under you between the check and the deploy.
